description.value: You become trained in advanced weapons, and you gain Tally and Redline as the Deadhand class defines them. Your Tally cap is 2, not the class’s 5, and it fills only when you drop a foe — not from eating a critical hit and staying up, and not from a turn spent below half. You do not get the clean first Redline: every Redline you spend rolls on the Slip table, starting with the first one. Twenty years is what buys the free one, and you have not put in twenty years.

cinderfall.incomplete: Trained in advanced weapons is implemented. Tally and Redline (including the Tally cap of 2, fill-only-on-a-kill condition, and the forced Slip-table roll on every Redline spend) are Cinderfall's own class-resource subsystem with no counterpart anywhere in the actor schema or rule-element vocabulary -- there is no generic 'resource pool' rule element, only the class-specific ones core classes hardcode in engine code.
